stories.title: scrolling when inside the box changes the nymber
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 381660b5-e5dd-4d63-80be-ad8111e55663 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "scrolling when inside the box changes the nymber" (typo: "number")

When a numeric input in Settings (Timer or Projects tabs) is focused and the user scrolls with trackpad/mouse wheel to navigate the page, the browser's default `<input type="number">` behavior intercepts the wheel event and silently increments/decrements the value. The user meant to scroll the page but accidentally changed a timer duration, repetition count, or auto-archive value.

## Repro

1. Settings → Timer.
2. Click any numeric input (cookie break min/hr, default repetitions, break duration, long-break interval, long-break duration).
3. Scroll with the trackpad without clicking away.
4. The number changes instead of (or in addition to) the page scrolling.

Same in Settings → Projects → Archive for the auto-archive value input.

## Expected

Scrolling the settings panel over a number input scrolls the page, never changes the value. Values change only by typing or arrow keys.

## Root cause (verified)

No `<input type="number">` in the renderer has an `onWheel` handler (`grep -rn 'onWheel'` returns empty). All seven affected inputs @ HEAD d4c9f69:

- `src/renderer/src/features/settings/TimerSettingsContent.tsx:251` — Cookie break min/hr
- `TimerSettingsContent.tsx:294` — Default repetitions
- `TimerSettingsContent.tsx:311` — Break duration (min)
- `TimerSettingsContent.tsx:347` — Long break every N sessions
- `TimerSettingsContent.tsx:364` — Long break duration (min)
- `src/renderer/src/features/settings/ProjectsSettingsContent.tsx:793` — Auto-archive value
- `src/renderer/src/shared/components/TimerPlayButton.tsx:306` — Start-dialog Reps (lower risk: non-scrolling popup, same underlying issue)

The settings content area is scrollable: `UnifiedSettingsModal.tsx:127` — `<div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto pr-3">`.

## Fix plan

Add `onWheel={(e) => e.currentTarget.blur()}` to all seven `<input type="number">` elements listed above:

```tsx
<input type="number" ... onWheel={(e) => e.currentTarget.blur()} />
```

`blur()` is the canonical approach: page scroll keeps working, the input just deselects. (`preventDefault()` would block page scrolling too.)

## Edge cases

- Keyboard up/down arrows still increment when focused — intentional.
- The native spin buttons are already hidden via `[appearance:textfield]` CSS, so there's no visual increment affordance lost.
- Blur triggers `onChange`/`onBlur` once with the unchanged value — no spurious writes.

## Tests

Manual only (one-liner DOM handler): reproduce the repro steps; after the fix the value must not change while scrolling.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — zero `onWheel` handlers exist in the renderer; all 7 number inputs are unprotected. (If the reported "box" was something other than these settings inputs, flag it — but these are the only `<input type="number">` elements in the app.)

stories.title: archive can't delete last number for settings. you have to select it and overwrite instead
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 7c8aefa0-3bcf-40a4-90ba-80286ca1e20d — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "archive can't delete last number for settings. you have to select it and overwrite instead"

In Settings → Projects → Archive tab, the "Auto-Archive after N days/hours" numeric input doesn't allow deleting the last digit. When all digits are erased the field instantly resets to `3` (the fallback), so you can never reach an empty state to type a fresh number. The only workaround is select-all-then-type.

## Repro

1. Settings → Projects → Archive subtab.
2. Enable auto-archive for any non-shared project.
3. Click the number input (shows `3`).
4. Press Backspace → the field instantly shows `3` again.

## Expected

The input allows an empty transient state while typing. The store write happens only on commit (blur) or when the value is a valid number.

## Root cause (verified)

`src/renderer/src/features/settings/ProjectsSettingsContent.tsx:797` (inside `ArchiveSection`, lines 773–834):

```tsx
value={project.auto_archive_value ?? 3}
onChange={(e) => updateProject(project.id, { auto_archive_value: parseInt(e.target.value, 10) || 3 })}
```

- Fully controlled from the Zustand store.
- On empty field, `parseInt("", 10)` is `NaN`, `NaN || 3` → `3`, `updateProject` fires immediately, store updates synchronously, React re-renders the input with `3` before the next keystroke.

## Fix plan

All in `ProjectsSettingsContent.tsx`, function `ArchiveSection`:

1. Add local display state:
   ```tsx
   const [localValues, setLocalValues] = useState<Record<string, string>>(() =>
     Object.fromEntries(projects.map((p) => [p.id, String(p.auto_archive_value ?? 3)]))
   )
   ```
2. Drive the input from local state; commit on blur with clamping:
   ```tsx
   <input
     type="number" min={1} max={999}
     value={localValues[project.id] ?? String(project.auto_archive_value ?? 3)}
     onChange={(e) => setLocalValues((prev) => ({ ...prev, [project.id]: e.target.value }))}
     onBlur={(e) => {
       const parsed = parseInt(e.target.value, 10)
       const clamped = isNaN(parsed) || parsed < 1 ? 1 : Math.min(parsed, 999)
       setLocalValues((prev) => ({ ...prev, [project.id]: String(clamped) }))
       updateProject(project.id, { auto_archive_value: clamped })
     }}
     className={/* keep existing classes */}
   />
   ```
3. Keep the unit `select` unchanged.
4. Sync new project IDs into `localValues` when the `projects` prop changes:
   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     setLocalValues((prev) => {
       const next = { ...prev }
       for (const p of projects) if (!(p.id in next)) next[p.id] = String(p.auto_archive_value ?? 3)
       return next
     })
   }, [projects])
   ```

## Edge cases

- `0`/negative → clamp to 1 on blur; `>999` → clamp to 999.
- Clear field + tab away → commits 1 (minimum), never empty/0.
- Two projects with auto-archive on: state is keyed by `project.id`, edits don't cross-contaminate.
- Auto-archive toggled off mid-edit: input unmounts; `localValues` lives in the parent — no cleanup needed.

## Tests

`ProjectsSettingsContent.test.tsx` (create next to source, @testing-library/react):
- Change event with `""` → input still shows `""` (not `3`); blur → `updateProject` called with `auto_archive_value: 1`.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — `ProjectsSettingsContent.tsx:797` has the `parseInt(...) || 3` write-on-every-keystroke pattern.

stories.title: clicking 'less' on an expanded projects list doesnt work
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 493d85fd-2c10-43b6-adfc-c560af68b84c — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "clicking 'less' on an expanded projects list doesnt work"

When the sidebar project list is expanded and the user clicks "Less", the list collapses for a split second and then immediately re-expands (or never visually collapses at all) whenever the currently selected project sits beyond position 5.

## Repro

1. Have more than 5 projects.
2. Click a project that appears only after clicking "More" (position ≥ 6 in sidebar order).
3. The list auto-expands to show that project.
4. Click "Less" → the list does not collapse.

## Expected

Clicking "Less" always collapses the list to the first 5 projects, regardless of which project is selected.

## Root cause (verified)

`src/renderer/src/features/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:230–236` — the auto-expand effect lists `projectsExpanded` in its dependency array:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (currentView !== 'project' || !selectedProjectId) return
  const idx = projects.findIndex((p) => p.id === selectedProjectId)
  if (idx >= MAX_VISIBLE_PROJECTS && !projectsExpanded) {
    setProjectsExpanded(true)
  }
}, [currentView, selectedProjectId, projects, projectsExpanded])  // ← projectsExpanded is the problem
```

Flow when the user clicks "Less" (button at Sidebar.tsx:417): `setProjectsExpanded(false)` → dependency `projectsExpanded` changed → effect re-runs → selected project is at `idx >= 5` and `!projectsExpanded` is now true → `setProjectsExpanded(true)` → back to expanded. Net effect: the click appears dead.

## Fix plan

1. **Sidebar.tsx:230–236** — remove `projectsExpanded` from the dependency array; read the current value via a ref so the effect only fires on navigation, never on manual toggle:

```ts
const projectsExpandedRef = useRef(projectsExpanded)
useEffect(() => { projectsExpandedRef.current = projectsExpanded }, [projectsExpanded])

useEffect(() => {
  if (currentView !== 'project' || !selectedProjectId) return
  const idx = projects.findIndex((p) => p.id === selectedProjectId)
  if (idx >= MAX_VISIBLE_PROJECTS && !projectsExpandedRef.current) {
    setProjectsExpanded(true)
  }
}, [currentView, selectedProjectId, projects])
```

2. No other files need changes.

## Edge cases

- Navigating away and back to a hidden project still auto-expands via the remaining dependencies. ✓
- Clicking "Less" then clicking a hidden project: navigation fires the effect → re-expands (correct).
- The ref-sync effect is a one-liner — no performance concern.

## Tests

File: `src/renderer/src/features/sidebar/Sidebar.test.tsx` (create next to Sidebar.tsx)
- Clicking "Less" collapses the list (selected project at index 7, list shrinks to 5 and stays).
- Auto-expand fires when navigating to a hidden project.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — Sidebar.tsx:230–236 includes `projectsExpanded` in the `useEffect` deps, re-expanding immediately after the user collapses.

stories.title: creating a new project should take the next color in line
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 3de51a1f-6cb4-4429-a43a-6561928be542 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

When creating a new project, pre-select the next palette color that isn't already used by an existing project (or cycle deterministically when all are used), instead of always defaulting to `#6366f1` (indigo).

## Why

Every new project currently starts indigo, requiring manual re-selection each time. Pre-advancing through the palette reduces friction and produces a visually varied project list by default.

## Current behavior (verified, file:line)

Two creation flows, both hardcode the first color:

- **`src/renderer/src/features/projects/NewProjectModal.tsx:12–19, 67, 78`** — local `PROJECT_COLORS` array (8 colors: `#6366f1, #8b5cf6, #ec4899, #ef4444, #f59e0b, #22c55e, #06b6d4, #3b82f6`); `useState(PROJECT_COLORS[0])`; resets to `PROJECT_COLORS[0]` after create and on close.
- **`src/renderer/src/features/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:112, 226, 372, 375`** — inline create form hardcodes `'#6366f1'` in three places and duplicates the palette literal at line 375 (not shared with the modal).

## Implementation guide

1. **Create `src/renderer/src/features/projects/projectColors.ts`:**
   ```ts
   export const PROJECT_COLORS = [
     '#6366f1', '#8b5cf6', '#ec4899', '#ef4444',
     '#f59e0b', '#22c55e', '#06b6d4', '#3b82f6'
   ]

   /** First color not used by any existing project; falls back to cycling by count. */
   export function pickNextProjectColor(existingColors: string[]): string {
     const used = new Set(existingColors.map((c) => c.toLowerCase()))
     const unused = PROJECT_COLORS.find((c) => !used.has(c.toLowerCase()))
     if (unused) return unused
     return PROJECT_COLORS[existingColors.length % PROJECT_COLORS.length]
   }
   ```
2. **`NewProjectModal.tsx`** — import from `projectColors.ts`, remove the local const, initialise with `useState(() => pickNextProjectColor(Object.values(allProjects).map(p => p.color)))`, and reset via the same helper after create / on close (read fresh store state via `useProjectStore.getState().projects` after the create call).
3. **`Sidebar.tsx`** — import `PROJECT_COLORS` + `pickNextProjectColor`; replace the inline palette literal (line 375) and all three hardcoded `'#6366f1'` occurrences (lines 112, 226, 372) with the helper applied to `projects.map(p => p.color)`.
4. No backend/IPC changes — color is a pure renderer concern, already passed through `createProject({ color, ... })`.

## Edge cases

- All 8 colors in use → deterministic cycling by `existingColors.length % 8`.
- Project deleted mid-session → next creation recalculates from current store state; freed color may be re-suggested.
- User can still manually change the color — the picker stays fully interactive.

## Tests

File: `src/renderer/src/features/projects/projectColors.test.ts`
- `pickNextProjectColor([])` → `'#6366f1'`
- `pickNextProjectColor(['#6366f1'])` → `'#8b5cf6'`
- `pickNextProjectColor(PROJECT_COLORS)` cycles by length
- Case-insensitive: `'#6366F1'` counts as used for `'#6366f1'`

## Acceptance criteria

1. Modal with no projects pre-selects `#6366f1`; with one indigo project pre-selects `#8b5cf6`.
2. After creating, reopening pre-selects the next unused color.
3. The sidebar inline form follows the same logic.
4. Both forms share `PROJECT_COLORS` from `projectColors.ts` (no duplicated literals).

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-not-implemented @ HEAD d4c9f69 — both `NewProjectModal.tsx:19` and `Sidebar.tsx:112` hardcode `#6366f1` with no palette-advance logic.

stories.title: shared projects are not visible until i click 'MORE' in the sidebar, even though they are higher in the order
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 6b762989-eeee-4e5b-b195-f69dfa5c5b43 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "shared projects are not visible until i click 'MORE' in the sidebar, even though they are higher in the order"

When a shared project arrives on a member's device (invite accepted / discovered via `discoverRemoteMemberships`), it is created locally with `sidebar_order = 0`, but on the next sync `applyRemote` overwrites `sidebar_order` with the OWNER's value — which can be a large integer reflecting the owner's own ordering. On the member's device this pushes the shared project past the 5-slot `MAX_VISIBLE_PROJECTS` cutoff, hiding it behind the "More" button even though the member never placed it there.

## Repro

1. User A has 6+ personal projects (sidebar_orders 0–5+).
2. User B has 5 personal projects (sidebar_orders 0–4).
3. User A shares project #6 (their `sidebar_order = 6`) with User B.
4. User B's app discovers and syncs the shared project down.
5. After the first subsequent sync, the shared project has `sidebar_order = 6` on B's device.
6. User B's sidebar slices to 5 visible; the shared project is hidden behind "More".

## Expected

A newly arriving shared project should append after the member's own projects (or at least not be silently placed beyond the visible cutoff). The member's local ordering should not be overwritten by the owner's ordering.

## Root cause (verified)

- `src/renderer/src/services/SyncService.ts:917–926` — initial creation of a discovered shared project does not pass `sidebar_order` → defaults to 0 (`ProjectRepository.ts:77`).
- `src/main/repositories/ProjectRepository.ts:191,209` — `applyRemote` overwrites `sidebar_order` with the remote (owner's) value on every sync:
  ```sql
  sidebar_order = excluded.sidebar_order,
  ```
  with `remote.sidebar_order ?? 0` as the bound value.
- `AppLayout.tsx:75–78` sorts projects by `sidebar_order`; `Sidebar.tsx:90, 299–302` slices to `MAX_VISIBLE_PROJECTS = 5` when not expanded.

## Fix plan

1. **`src/renderer/src/services/SyncService.ts:918`** — when creating a newly-discovered shared project locally, set `sidebar_order = maxLocalOrder + 1`:
   ```ts
   const localProjects = await window.api.projects.getProjectsForUser(userId)
   const maxLocalOrder = localProjects.reduce((m, p) => Math.max(m, p.sidebar_order ?? 0), -1)
   await window.api.projects.create({ ...existing fields..., sidebar_order: maxLocalOrder + 1 })
   ```
2. **`src/main/repositories/ProjectRepository.ts` — `applyRemote`** — treat `sidebar_order` as a local-only preference; do not overwrite an existing local value. Change the `ON CONFLICT UPDATE` clause (line 191) to:
   ```sql
   sidebar_order = COALESCE(projects.sidebar_order, excluded.sidebar_order),
   ```
   This preserves the member's order once set, falling back to the remote value only for brand-new rows.
3. No UI changes needed.

## Edge cases

- First sync with no local order: step 1 writes a correct initial value before `applyRemote` can fire.
- Existing project later becomes shared (`is_shared` flip): local `sidebar_order` already set — COALESCE preserves it.
- Drag-to-reorder in Settings → Projects (`updateSidebarOrder`) sets explicit ordering — preserved by step 2.

## Tests

File: `src/main/repositories/ProjectRepository.test.ts`
- `applyRemote does not overwrite existing sidebar_order`: create project locally with `sidebar_order = 2`, applyRemote with `sidebar_order = 99`, assert local row keeps 2.
- `applyRemote sets sidebar_order for new rows from remote value`.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — `applyRemote` (ProjectRepository.ts:191) overwrites `sidebar_order` unconditionally; `syncProjectDown` (SyncService.ts:918) does not pass `sidebar_order` on create. No fix in CHANGELOG or recent commits.

stories.title: adding a date, then deleting it from the 'labels' still adds the due date and removes the text from the title.
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: c18e314c-1d65-48b6-a553-f612e431dcea — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "adding a date, then deleting it from the 'labels' still adds the due date and removes the text from the title."

When the NLP date chip is shown in quick-add (e.g., user types "buy milk tomorrow") and the user clicks the × to dismiss it, the chip disappears but on submit:
1. The due date is still applied to the created task.
2. The date text (e.g., "tomorrow") is still stripped from the task title.

The same bug affects the in-app `AddTaskInput` component as it shares the same `useSmartInput` hook.

## Repro

1. Open quick-add (global shortcut).
2. Type `buy milk tomorrow`.
3. Observe the NLP date chip "tomorrow" appears.
4. Click the × button on that chip to dismiss it.
5. Observe the chip disappears.
6. Press Enter to submit.
7. Check the created task: title is "buy milk" (date text was stripped) and due_date is set to tomorrow (date was applied).

## Expected

- Dismissing the NLP chip communicates to the submit path that the user intentionally rejected the detected date.
- The task is created with the full original title ("buy milk tomorrow") and no due date.

## Root cause

`src/renderer/src/shared/hooks/useSmartInput.ts` lines 245–248 (`dismissNlpDate`):
```ts
const dismissNlpDate = useCallback(() => {
  setNlpDateResult(null)
  nlpDismissedRef.current = true
}, [])
```

`useSmartInput.ts` lines 288–296 (`getSubmitData`):
```ts
const freshNlp = (!selectedDate && !title.includes('d:')) ? parseNlpDate(title) : null
const effectiveNlp = freshNlp ?? nlpDateResult
// ...
if (effectiveNlp && !selectedDate) {
  title = stripDateFromTitle(title, effectiveNlp)
  nlpDate = formatNlpDate(effectiveNlp)
```

`getSubmitData` calls `parseNlpDate(title)` unconditionally (ignoring `nlpDismissedRef.current`). Because the input text is not modified when the chip is dismissed, the fresh parse re-detects the same date. `effectiveNlp` becomes non-null, the date is applied, and the text is stripped.

`nlpDismissedRef.current` is consulted only in `handleInputChange` (line 118), never in `getSubmitData`.

## Fix plan

All changes are in a single file: `src/renderer/src/shared/hooks/useSmartInput.ts`

1. **Honour the dismissed flag in `getSubmitData`.** Change the guard at line 290 from:
   ```ts
   const freshNlp = (!selectedDate && !title.includes('d:')) ? parseNlpDate(title) : null
   ```
   to:
   ```ts
   const freshNlp = (!selectedDate && !title.includes('d:') && !nlpDismissedRef.current)
     ? parseNlpDate(title)
     : null
   ```
   This ensures a dismissed NLP chip is honoured at submit time even when `nlpDateResult` state has already been cleared.

2. The `freshNlp ?? nlpDateResult` fallback (line 291) needs no further change — after the guard above, `freshNlp` will be `null` when dismissed, and `nlpDateResult` is also `null` (cleared by `dismissNlpDate`).

3. `nlpDismissedRef` is a `useRef` (stable object) — no `useCallback` dependency-array change needed.

No IPC, preload, store, or component layer changes are needed — the fix is entirely within the hook.

## Edge cases

- If the user dismisses the chip and then types more text containing another date phrase, the `nlpDismissedRef.current = true` flag suppresses NLP until `reset()` — existing intended behaviour, no change required.
- The `d:` operator path with a confirmed chip (`selectedDate !== null`) is unaffected (the `!selectedDate` guard keeps it separate).
- `AddTaskInput.tsx` shares `useSmartInput` and automatically benefits from the fix.

## Tests

Test file: `src/renderer/src/shared/hooks/useSmartInput.test.ts` (create alongside `useSmartInput.ts` if absent).

```ts
it('getSubmitData returns no nlpDate after dismissNlpDate is called', () => {
  const inputRef = { current: null } as React.RefObject<HTMLInputElement | null>
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useSmartInput(inputRef))
  act(() => { result.current.handleInputChange('buy milk tomorrow', 18) })
  expect(result.current.nlpDateResult).not.toBeNull()
  act(() => { result.current.dismissNlpDate() })
  expect(result.current.nlpDateResult).toBeNull()
  const data = result.current.getSubmitData()
  expect(data.nlpDate).toBeNull()
  expect(data.title).toBe('buy milk tomorrow')
})
```

stories.title: why does adding ' 121s' set a date?
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 7a6830d9-9ebd-46d5-b4d7-41caf4d30cc0 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "why does adding ' 121s' set a date?"

Typing a task name that ends in a number followed by one of `s m h d w y` (e.g., "fix bug 121s", "deploy in 5m", "API v2h") causes an NLP date chip to appear and, if submitted without dismissing, sets a due date on the created task. chrono-node's casual parser interprets `NNs` as "NN seconds from now", `NNm` as minutes, `NNh` hours, `NNd` days, `NNw` weeks, `NNy` years. This produces false positives for code-related task names, version strings, and ticket IDs.

## Repro

1. Open quick-add.
2. Type `fix bug 121s`.
3. Observe an NLP date chip appears ("121s", a time a few minutes in the future).
4. Press Enter — task is created with a due date.

Also reproducible with: `deploy 5m`, `close 2h`, `update config 3d`, `migrate data 2w`, `update node 2y`.

**Single-token inputs like just `121s` are already correctly suppressed** by the 80% filter (chip suppressed when matched text covers ≥80% of input length, `useSmartInput.ts:121`), but multi-word inputs are not.

## Expected

Bare time abbreviations of the form `\d+[smhdwy]` appearing as a standalone token (not preceded by "in") should not trigger a date chip. "fix bug 121s" should produce no chip. Intentional relative durations remain available via "in 5m" / "in 121s".

## Root cause

`src/shared/nlpDateParser.ts` line 123:
```ts
const results = chrono.parse(text, ref, { forwardDate: true })
```
`chrono.parse` is the casual parser, which includes a relative-duration parser recognising `NNs/NNm/NNh/NNd/NNw/NNy` as standalone expressions. `chrono.strict.parse` doesn't fire this parser but also rejects "tomorrow"/"next friday", so switching modes wholesale would break the feature.

Confirmed with the installed chrono-node 2.9.0:
- `chrono.casual.parse('task 121s', ref)` → `[{ text: '121s', date: <now + 121s> }]`
- `chrono.strict.parse('task 121s', ref)` → `[]` (but also drops 'tomorrow')

The 80% guard in `useSmartInput.ts:121` only suppresses the chip when the matched substring covers ≥80% of the input — multi-word task names pass through.

## Fix plan

All changes in `src/shared/nlpDateParser.ts`.

1. **Reject bare relative-duration matches post-parse.** In `parseNlpDate()`, immediately after `const results = chrono.parse(text, ref, { forwardDate: true })` (line 123), before the return at lines 127–136:
   ```ts
   if (results.length > 0) {
     const r = results[0]
     // Reject bare relative duration abbreviations: NNs / NNm / NNh / NNd / NNw / NNy.
     // False positives for code/ticket names; intentional uses appear as "in NNs" etc.
     if (/^\d+[smhdwy]$/i.test(r.text.trim())) return null
     ...
   }
   ```
2. **Apply the same guard to the normalized-text branch** (lines 105–119, used when written numbers are present): after `const r = normResults[0]`, add the same `if (/^\d+[smhdwy]$/i.test(r.text.trim())) return null`.

The regex matches only bare single-token abbreviations. It does NOT match:
- `3pm` / `9am` (two-char suffix)
- `in 5m` / `in 2h` (matched text starts with "in ")
- `tomorrow`, `next friday` (no digit prefix)
- `0.5h` / `2.5h` (decimal point before the unit)

## Edge cases

- "in 5m" / "in 121s": chrono matches the full phrase including "in" — regex fails → still parses. ✓
- "5m" alone: already blocked by the 80% filter; the new guard adds a second layer.
- `3d` shorthand users: blocked consistently; type "in 3d" or "in 3 days" instead.

## Tests

Add to `src/shared/nlpDateParser.test.ts` in the `describe('parseNlpDate')` block:

```ts
it('no false positive for bare "121s"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('fix bug 121s', ref)).toBeNull() })
it('no false positive for "5m"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('deploy code 5m', ref)).toBeNull() })
it('no false positive for "2h"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('close issue 2h', ref)).toBeNull() })
it('no false positive for "3d"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('update 3d', ref)).toBeNull() })
it('still parses "in 5m"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('remind me in 5m', ref)).not.toBeNull() })
it('still parses "in 121s"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('alert in 121s', ref)).not.toBeNull() })
it('still parses "tomorrow"', () => { expect(parseNlpDate('call Alice tomorrow', ref)).not.toBeNull() })
```

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — `parseNlpDate` (`src/shared/nlpDateParser.ts:123`) uses casual chrono mode with no guard against bare `\d+[smhdwy]` tokens. Behaviour confirmed by running chrono-node 2.9.0 directly.

stories.title: creating labels from inside a project doesnt actually work
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: ccca14d1-b081-4be6-b1f1-c78e88e138a6 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "creating labels from inside a project doesnt actually work"

Creating a label from the LabelPicker inside a project ("+ New label…") creates the label globally and links it to the project **locally only**. The `project_labels` junction row is never pushed to Supabase. On the same device everything looks fine; on a second device (or after a full reconcile) the label exists globally but is NOT linked to the project — missing from that project's FilterBar/LabelPicker.

## Repro

1. Open any project → open the LabelPicker on a task.
2. "+ New label…", enter a name, Create.
3. Same device: label appears in FilterBar/picker — looks correct.
4. Sign in on a second device (or force a full reconcile).
5. Bug: label visible globally (Settings → Labels) but absent from the project's FilterBar — the `project_labels` link never reached Supabase.

## Expected

Creating a label inside a project context must push BOTH the `user_labels` row AND the `project_labels` junction row to Supabase.

## Root cause (verified)

`labelStore.createLabel()` (`src/renderer/src/shared/stores/labelStore.ts:150–178`) only calls `pushLabel(label, userId)` — it never calls `pushProjectLabel(projectId, labelId, null)`:

```ts
// labelStore.ts:168-171 — only pushes the label row, not the junction:
import('../../services/PersonalSyncService').then(({ pushLabel }) => {
  pushLabel(label, getUserId()).catch(() => {})
})
// Missing: pushProjectLabel(input.project_id, label.id, null)
```

The local SQLite side is correct: `LabelRepository.create()` (`src/main/repositories/LabelRepository.ts:122–125`) calls `this.addToProject(project_id, id)` when `project_id` is set.

The `useCreateOrMatchLabel` hook (`src/renderer/src/shared/hooks/useCreateOrMatchLabel.ts:28–33`) takes the new-label path via `createLabel({..., project_id})`. The store's `addToProject` action (line ~326) — the only path that calls `pushProjectLabel` — is exercised only when an EXISTING label is added to a project, not on creation.

## Fix plan

1. **`labelStore.ts` — `createLabel` action (~line 169):** after `pushLabel`, also push the junction when `input.project_id` is set:
   ```ts
   if (input.project_id) {
     const { pushProjectLabel } = await import('../../services/PersonalSyncService')
     void pushProjectLabel(input.project_id, label.id, null)
   }
   ```
   Use dynamic import (same pattern as `addToProject` at line 326) to avoid circular dependency.
2. No schema change — Supabase `project_labels` already exists with `deleted_at` support.
3. No migration — local SQLite already creates the row.

## Edge cases

- Offline / `pushLabel` fails: `pushProjectLabel` would hit FK 23503, which it already handles gracefully (logs + skips since commit 72097f6). No special handling needed.
- The existing-label path via `addToProject` already pushes correctly — only the new-label path is broken.
- `LabelSettingsContent` creates labels without `project_id` — unaffected.

## Tests

- Store-level test (mock PersonalSyncService): create a label with `project_id` → assert `pushProjectLabel` called with `(projectId, labelId, null)`.
- Existing `repositories.test.ts` covers the local create+link.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — chain TaskListView → LabelPicker → `useCreateOrMatchLabel` → `labelStore.createLabel` never calls `pushProjectLabel`.

stories.title: start timer context menu doesn't show flow timer when it is enabled in settings
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 1a17c4fc-5a21-4b4c-9fcb-c9ab6e719419 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "start timer context menu doesn't show flow timer when it is enabled in settings"

Right-click a task → "Start Timer" → the submenu shows duration presets only and always starts a standard countdown — even when Settings → Timer → Default mode is **Flowtime**. The task-row play button (▶) handles Flowtime correctly; the context-menu path ignores the setting.

## Repro

1. Settings → Timer → Default mode → **Flowtime**.
2. Right-click any task → Start Timer → click any preset.
3. The timer starts as a countdown (no flowtime/count-up, no cookie pool).

## Expected

With flowtime as the default mode, the context-menu path starts a Flowtime timer (`isFlowtime: true`, cookie pool active), mirroring `TimerPlayButton`.

## Root cause (verified)

`TimerSubmenu.handleStart` in `src/renderer/src/shared/components/ContextMenuSubmenus.tsx:317–339`:
```ts
const handleStart = useCallback((minutes: number) => {
  if (!currentUser || isRunning) return
  autoMoveToInProgress()
  const isInfinite = settings.defaultDuration === 'infinite'
  startTimer({
    taskId, taskTitle, minutes,
    reps: isInfinite ? 1 : settings.defaultReps,
    isPerpetual: isInfinite,
    breakMinutes: settings.breakMinutes,
    // ❌ isFlowtime never set — always false
    // ❌ cookieMinutesPerHour never passed — always 0
  })
  onClose()
}, ...)
```
History: Gabriel's play-button bug (task 9a6f6ddb, Done) was fixed in commit `aa5d8c4` (2026-04-26) — `TimerPlayButton.tsx:58–81` now uses `paramsToStoreArgs()` which derives `isFlowtime` from `settings.defaultMode` and passes `cookieMinutesPerHour`. That commit touched `ContextMenuSubmenus.tsx` too but only updated reps/isPerpetual — the flowtime branch was missed. `startTimer` (`timerStore.ts:94`) already accepts `isFlowtime?: boolean` and `cookieMinutesPerHour?: number`.

## Fix plan

1. **`ContextMenuSubmenus.tsx` — `handleStart` (line 317):**
   - `const isFlowtime = settings.defaultMode === 'flowtime'`
   - Pass `isFlowtime` and `cookieMinutesPerHour: isFlowtime ? settings.cookieMinutesPerHour : 0` to `startTimer`.
   - When `isFlowtime`: `reps: 0`, `isPerpetual: false` (mirror `paramsToStoreArgs`, `TimerPlayButton.tsx:24–26`).
2. **Submenu UI (lines 341–361):** when `defaultMode === 'flowtime'`, show a single "Start Flowtime" entry (count-up ignores preset durations; optionally keep presets labelled "Stop after Xm" as a soft target). When in timer mode, keep the current preset list.
3. No changes to `ContextMenu.tsx` flyout wiring (246–248) or `timerStore.ts`.

## Edge cases

- `skipStartDialog` is play-button-only; the submenu already fires directly — no interaction.
- Timer already running: the submenu already disables itself (343–344) — preserve.
- `cookieMinutesPerHour` must be 0 in non-flowtime mode.

## Tests

- New `ContextMenuSubmenus.test.ts` (or extend `TimerPlayButton.test.ts`): with `defaultMode === 'flowtime'`, `TimerSubmenu.handleStart` passes `isFlowtime: true` and `cookieMinutesPerHour > 0` to `startTimer`.
- Regression: existing flowtime+infinite test in `TimerPlayButton.test.ts` keeps passing.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

stories.title: add color to tray my day according to maybe priority?
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 4c9e9266-70f8-431f-8967-8bbd510aec6a — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Add a small priority-colored dot icon to each task entry in the macOS tray's My Day menu, so urgent/high tasks are visible at a glance without opening the app.

## Why

Priority already drives visuals everywhere in the app (chips, row indicators). Surfacing it in the tray makes the menu useful for triage: with 10 tasks listed, the 2 urgent ones jump out.

## Current behavior (verified)

- `src/main/tray.ts` — `buildLeftClickMenu` (lines 125–178) builds **text-only** menu items: `label: \`${icon} ${truncateTitle(task.title)}\`` where `icon` is a Unicode ○/◑ from `STATUS_ICONS` (`tray-utils.ts:25–29`). No `icon` property on any item.
- `TrayTask` (`src/main/tray-utils.ts:5–9`) carries only `{ id, title, bucket }` — **no `priority` field** — though `classifyMyDayTasks` (line 31+) has the full `Task` objects available.
- `nativeImage` is already imported in `tray.ts:1` (tray icon only). Electron's `MenuItemConstructorOptions.icon` accepts a `NativeImage` rendered per item in native macOS menus.
- Priority palette (`PriorityIndicator.tsx:3–9`): 0=`#888888` (none), 1=`#22c55e`, 2=`#3b82f6`, 3=`#f59e0b`, 4=`#ef4444`.

## Implementation guide

1. **`tray-utils.ts`** — add `priority: number` to `TrayTask`; carry it through in `classifyMyDayTasks` (lines 52–55):
   ```ts
   ...notStarted.map((t) => ({ id: t.id, title: t.title, bucket: 'not_started' as const, priority: t.priority })),
   ```
2. **Priority-dot icon factory** — new `src/main/priority-icons.ts` (or in tray-utils):
   ```ts
   const PRIORITY_DOT_B64: Record<number, string> = {
     1: '<base64 16x16 green-circle PNG>', 2: '<blue>', 3: '<amber>', 4: '<red>'
   }
   export function getPriorityDotIcon(priority: number): Electron.NativeImage | undefined {
     const b64 = PRIORITY_DOT_B64[priority]
     return b64 ? nativeImage.createFromBuffer(Buffer.from(b64, 'base64')) : undefined
   }
   ```
   Generating the PNGs: simplest zero-dependency option is embedding pre-generated base64 PNG constants (a 16×16 solid-circle PNG per color; even a 1×1 solid-color PNG of 67 bytes works since Electron scales it — though a real circle on transparent background looks better). For Retina sharpness use a 32×32 source with `createFromBuffer(buf, { scaleFactor: 2.0 })`. Don't add npm deps for this.
3. **`tray.ts` — `buildLeftClickMenu` (lines 155–162):**
   ```ts
   const priorityIcon = getPriorityDotIcon(task.priority)
   const item: Electron.MenuItemConstructorOptions = {
     label: `${statusIcon} ${truncateTitle(task.title)}`,
     click: () => navigateToTask(task.id)
   }
   if (priorityIcon) item.icon = priorityIcon
   menuItems.push(item)
   ```

## Edge cases

- Priority 0 (None) → no icon, label unchanged — keeps the menu clean.
- Per-item icons are independent of the tray icon's template-image mode; do NOT mark the dots as template images (they'd lose their colour).
- No settings toggle initially; add one only if the dots feel noisy.

## Tests

- `tray-utils.test.ts`: `classifyMyDayTasks` carries `priority` through to `TrayTask` (update the existing `makeTask` fixtures).
- `getPriorityDotIcon`: priorities 1–4 → NativeImage; 0 → undefined.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tray My Day entries show green/blue/amber/red dots for priorities 1–4; none for priority 0
- [ ] Status prefix (○/◑) and truncated title unchanged
- [ ] Existing tray-utils tests pass

stories.title: sort options for 'done' tasks per project. respect the default setting or sort by completed
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: f0f90144-da92-4bee-a778-4d3d13cff942 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Better sorting for Done (completed) tasks in the project view:
1. Add `completed_date` as a sort field in the sort picker.
2. (Optional enhancement) Auto-sort the Done section by `completed_date` descending when the project is on default custom sort — most recently completed first.

## Why

Done sections accumulate; the current `order_index` order reflects completion order only incidentally (via the `new_task_position` setting at status-change time). Users want most-recently-completed first, or an explicit "Completed" sort.

## Current behavior (verified)

- `TaskListView.tsx:817–824` — Done-status sections use the SAME `prioritySortFn` as every other section:
  ```ts
  const statusTasks = filteredTasks.filter(
    (t) => t.status_id === status.id && t.is_archived === 0 && t.is_template === 0
  ).sort(prioritySortFn)
  ```
- `prioritySortFn` (lines 247–254): `createSortComparator(sortRules, statusOrderMap)` when a non-custom sort is active, else pure `order_index`.
- `src/renderer/src/shared/utils/sortTasks.ts:3` — `SortField` has NO `'completed_date'`:
  ```ts
  export type SortField = 'priority' | 'due_date' | 'status' | 'created_at' | 'updated_at' | 'title' | 'project' | 'custom'
  ```
- `completed_date` exists on `Task` (types.ts:72; in `TASK_UPDATABLE_COLUMNS` types.ts:246), set when a task moves to a done status.

## Implementation guide

1. **`sortTasks.ts`** — add `'completed_date'` to `SortField`; add to `SORT_FIELD_LABELS` (`completed_date: 'Completed'`); add the compare case (nulls last):
   ```ts
   case 'completed_date':
     if (!a.completed_date && !b.completed_date) return 0
     if (!a.completed_date) return 1
     if (!b.completed_date) return -1
     return a.completed_date.localeCompare(b.completed_date)
   ```
2. **Sort picker** — options render from `SORT_FIELD_LABELS`, so "Completed" appears automatically.
3. **(Optional) Done-section default** — in `TaskListView.tsx`:
   ```ts
   const doneSortFn = useMemo(() => {
     if (!isCustomSort) return prioritySortFn       // explicit sort wins
     return (a: Task, b: Task): number => {
       if (a.completed_date && b.completed_date)
         return b.completed_date.localeCompare(a.completed_date)  // desc
       return a.order_index - b.order_index
     }
   }, [isCustomSort, prioritySortFn])
   ```
   In the render loop (817–824): `const comparator = status.is_done === 1 ? doneSortFn : prioritySortFn`. Apply the same in the `flatTasks` memo (264–273) so keyboard-nav order matches the rendered order.
4. **Drag handling** — when the done-section override sorts by `completed_date`, pass `disableDrag={true}` for done sections (consistent with the existing `disableDrag={!isCustomSort || isOfflineShared}` pattern — see debug-learnings.md "Sort applied at parent but child re-sorts internally").

## Edge cases

- `completed_date = null` in a done status (legacy/sync rows): sort last.
- Re-opened tasks (completed_date cleared): fall back to `order_index` — correct.
- `flatTasks` keyboard order must match render order — apply the comparator in both places.
- SavedView/MyDay have no done-section concept — no changes there.

## Tests

- `createSortComparator([{ field: 'completed_date', direction: 'desc' }])` sorts correctly, nulls last.
- Integration: complete two tasks in sequence → done section shows most-recent first (with optional override active).
- `flatTasks` order matches rendered order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Completed" available in the sort picker
- [ ] (Optional) Done section auto-sorts by completed_date desc under custom sort
- [ ] Drag disabled in done section when the override is active
- [ ] Keyboard navigation order matches the visual order

stories.title: 'go to task' when a new recurring task instance was created doesn't scroll into view
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: b1f620ae-f852-4db7-bef3-f45686016872 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "'go to task' when a new recurring task instance was created doesn't scroll into view"

Completing a recurring task shows a toast "Recurring task created → due {date}" with a "Go to task" button. Clicking it navigates to the right project and selects the new instance, but never scrolls the list — if the task is below the fold, nothing appears to happen.

## Repro

1. Recurring task with `recurrence_rule` + `due_date` in a project with more tasks than fit the viewport.
2. Mark it done → toast appears.
3. Click "Go to task" → project opens / selection set, but the viewport doesn't move to the task.

## Expected

"Go to task" navigates, selects, AND scrolls the new instance into view.

## Root cause (verified)

Toast action at `src/renderer/src/AppLayout.tsx:437–458`:
```ts
onClick: () => {
  if (cloneProjectId !== selectedProject?.id) {
    const proj = sortedProjects.find((p) => p.id === cloneProjectId)
    if (proj) useViewStore.getState().setSelectedProject(proj.id)  // navigates, clears selection
  }
  useTaskStore.getState().selectTask(taskId)   // selects — but NO scrollIntoView
}
```
- No `scrollIntoView` anywhere in this path. The only scroll implementations live INSIDE `TaskListView` via its `containerRef` (`handleStatusChange` at TaskListView.tsx:365–370 and keyboard nav at 524–528) — inaccessible from AppLayout.
- Cross-project case is worse: after `setSelectedProject`, the target view hasn't rendered yet (`hydrateAllForProject` is async), so even an immediate scroll would find no `[data-task-id]` element.

## Fix plan (pending-scroll pattern)

1. **`taskStore.ts`** — add `pendingScrollTaskId: string | null` + `setPendingScrollTask(id: string | null)` action.
2. **`AppLayout.tsx:444–453`** — after `selectTask(taskId)`, call `setPendingScrollTask(taskId)`. Also add it to the notification navigate handler (~143–147) and tray navigate handler (~128–134) for consistency.
3. **`TaskListView.tsx`** — consume it once the element exists:
   ```ts
   const pendingScrollTaskId = useTaskStore((s) => s.pendingScrollTaskId)
   useEffect(() => {
     if (!pendingScrollTaskId) return
     const raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
       const el = containerRef.current?.querySelector(`[data-task-id="${pendingScrollTaskId}"]`)
       if (el) {
         el.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' })
         useTaskStore.getState().setPendingScrollTask(null)
       }
     })
     return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf)
   }, [pendingScrollTaskId, flatTasks])  // flatTasks dep: re-runs after async hydration renders the row
   ```

## Edge cases

- Cross-project: the `flatTasks` dependency re-runs the effect after hydration; the pending id is only cleared once the element is actually found.
- Clear after one use to avoid re-scrolling on later renders.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (use `behavior: 'auto'` under `motion-safe` check if desired).

## Tests

- `selectTask` + pending scroll: `scrollIntoView` called on the `[data-task-id]` element; `pendingScrollTaskId` reset to null afterwards.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code @ HEAD d4c9f69 — AppLayout.tsx:437–458 has no scroll logic; no pending-scroll mechanism exists.

stories.title: add 'go to task' in views
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: f1f6a8cb-034b-47f2-bf99-44cd67abe99d — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Add a "Go to Task" context-menu item for task rows in Saved Views (and optionally Calendar), mirroring the existing My Day implementation. It navigates to the task's home project and selects the task there.

## Why

In a saved view (cross-project filter) you can't jump to a task's source project to see it in context, drag it between statuses, or use project-specific actions. My Day already has this; Saved Views should have parity.

## Current behavior (verified)

`src/renderer/src/shared/components/ContextMenu.tsx:175–187` — the item is gated behind `isMyDay`:
```tsx
const isMyDay = currentView === 'my-day'   // line 50

{isMyDay && task.project_id && (
  <MenuItem icon={<ExternalLink size={14} />} label="Go to Task"
    onClick={() => { handleAction(() => {
      useViewStore.getState().setSelectedProject(task.project_id)
      useTaskStore.getState().selectTask(task.id)
    }) }} />
)}
```
`SavedViewListView.tsx:409–430` renders `TaskRow`, whose right-click opens this shared `ContextMenu`; with `currentView === 'saved-view'`, `isMyDay` is false → the item never appears. The navigation action itself is view-agnostic and would work as-is.

## Implementation guide

1. **`ContextMenu.tsx`** — broaden the guard:
   ```tsx
   const showGoToTask = (currentView === 'my-day' || currentView === 'saved-view') && task.project_id
   ```
   and use `{showGoToTask && (...)}` for the existing MenuItem (lines ~175–187). Optionally include `'calendar'`.
2. **Scroll into view** — once task b1f620ae's `pendingScrollTaskId` mechanism exists, also call `useTaskStore.getState().setPendingScrollTask(task.id)` in the onClick so the row actually scrolls into view after navigation.
3. **Guard against missing projects** — before navigating, check `useProjectStore.getState().projects[task.project_id]` exists (task could belong to an archived/deleted project); skip or toast if not.
4. No changes needed in `SavedViewListView.tsx` — the shared ContextMenu reads `currentView` from the view store.

## Edge cases

- Task from the currently open project appearing in a saved view: navigation still useful (exits the saved-view context) — keep the item visible.
- Hidden in project views (redundant there).
- Existing My Day behavior unchanged.

## Tests

- Render ContextMenu with `currentView='saved-view'` → "Go to Task" present.
- `currentView='project'` → absent.
- Click → `setSelectedProject(task.project_id)` + `selectTask(task.id)` called.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Right-click in a Saved View shows "Go to Task"
- [ ] Click navigates to the task's project and selects (and scrolls to, if b1f620ae landed) the task
- [ ] Hidden in project views; My Day unchanged

stories.title: add a labels filter on top of views that shows all the labels of the currently shown tasks in that view!
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 8b6b6b3d-4d59-4352-a7eb-315e699e5d62 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Show inline label chips above the task list in SavedViewListView ("views") listing only the labels present on the currently visible tasks; clicking a chip filters by that label. This already exists in My Day — Saved Views is the gap.

## Why

The saved-views screen is the cross-project hub; labels are the primary slicing mechanism. Users want one-click label filtering scoped to what's actually visible, not a global label list buried in the "+ Filter" dropdown.

## Current behavior (verified 2026-06-10)

| View | Label chips inline? | Scoped to visible tasks? |
|---|---|---|
| TaskListView (project) | Yes — FilterBar with `labels={allProjectLabels}` (TaskListView.tsx:803) | No — all project labels |
| SavedViewListView | **No** — `labelsInFilterMenu=true` hides chips in the + Filter dropdown (SavedViewListView.tsx:391–398) | No — all user labels (`deduplicateLabelsByName(rawAllLabels, userId)`) |
| MyDayView | Yes — FilterBar with `labels={labelsInUse}` (line 830) | **Yes** — `labelsInUse` computed from My Day tasks (lines 197–207) |

`LabelFilterBar` (`src/renderer/src/shared/components/LabelFilterBar.tsx`) exists but is wired into **no** view — dead code; either reuse or delete it.

## Implementation guide

1. **SavedViewListView — compute labels from visible tasks.** In `src/renderer/src/features/views/SavedViewListView.tsx`, after the `matchingTasks` memo (lines 237–273):
   ```ts
   const labelsInView = useMemo(() => {
     const usedIds = new Set<string>()
     for (const t of matchingTasks) for (const l of taskLabels[t.id] ?? []) usedIds.add(l.id)
     return allLabels.filter((l) => usedIds.has(l.id))
   }, [matchingTasks, taskLabels, allLabels])
   ```
2. **Show chips inline.** Change the FilterBar usage (lines 391–398): drop `labelsInFilterMenu`, pass `labels={labelsInView}`:
   ```tsx
   <FilterBar labels={labelsInView} showProjectFilter showSort
     onSave={filtersChanged ? handleUpdateView : undefined}
     saveLabel={filtersChanged ? 'Save' : undefined} />
   ```
   This renders chips inline — same code path as TaskListView and MyDayView.
3. **TaskListView (optional, lower priority):** scope its chips to visible-task labels the same way for consistency; showing all project labels is also defensible.
4. **LabelFilterBar:** either wire it in (if a minimal chip-only row is preferred) or delete it as dead code.

## Edge cases

- `matchingTasks` empty → `labelsInView` empty → FilterBar returns `null` (FilterBar.tsx:223 guard) → no bar. Correct.
- Stacked filters: `matchingTasks` already accounts for active filters, so the chip list narrows automatically as filters stack.
- Cross-project saved views: `allLabels` already uses `deduplicateLabelsByName` — correct.

## Tests

- Unit: `labelsInView` memo — given `matchingTasks` + `taskLabels`, assert correct label set.
- Integration: tasks in two projects with different labels → saved view → only visible-task labels appear as chips.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a saved view shows inline chips for labels on the visible tasks
- [ ] Clicking a chip activates the label filter (same as project view)
- [ ] No chip row when no visible task has labels
- [ ] Stacking filters narrows the chip list
- [ ] + Filter and Sort buttons keep working alongside the chips

## Status check (2026-06-10)

PARTIALLY implemented — MyDayView already behaves as requested; SavedViewListView is the main gap (chips hidden in dropdown, not scoped); TaskListView shows all project labels inline.

stories.title: Saved view sidebar counts + open views don't auto-update when a task starts matching the filter
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 62df0d2c-6264-4d7c-be47-1fc7d847a139 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

The sidebar count next to a saved view, and the contents of an open saved view, don't refresh when a task starts (or stops) matching the view's filter — whether the task was created/edited locally in another view, or arrived remotely via MCP/another device. Counts only become correct at app restart, or when opening/leaving the saved view screen.

## Verified mechanics (2026-06-10 @ HEAD d4c9f69)

**Sidebar counts — a refresh-trigger bug, NOT a sync bug.** The data is already in local SQLite; nobody recounts:
- `savedViewStore.hydrateCounts` (`savedViewStore.ts:45–56`) → IPC `savedViews:countMatching` (`ipc-handlers.ts:1222`) → `SavedViewRepository.countMatchingTasks` (`SavedViewRepository.ts:183`) — one SQL count per view.
- Only call sites: `savedViewStore.hydrate` (app start, line 39), SavedViewListView's view-unmount cleanup (~line 180), and `handleUpdateView` after saving filters (~line 212).
- NO recount on: task create/complete/edit, label assign/remove, Realtime arrivals, or the WAL `tasks-changed` event.

**Open saved view — reactive, but with two data gaps:**
- `matchingTasks` is derived live from `useTaskStore(s => s.tasks)` + `taskLabels` (SavedViewListView.tsx:53–54, 239–273) → updates instantly IF the store contains the task and its labels.
- Gap A: the view only calls `hydrateAllLabels()` on mount (line 98) — it never hydrates **tasks** for projects not yet visited this session, so `allTasks` may simply lack matching tasks from unvisited projects. (Verify what App.tsx hydrates at login — likely only the current project via `hydrateAllForProject`.)
- Gap B (remote): a task row arrives live via the Realtime `tasks` subscription, but its **label assignments don't** (`task_labels` has no live path — see task 4c89a910, confirmed live 2026-06-10). Label-filtered views (most saved views) can't match the task until the next reconcile/restart.

## Answer to "can this be solved with subscribe?"

Only partially. Realtime subscribe fixes Gap B (remote label matching — already specced as 4c89a910 Part 3, the per-task `task_labels` targeted pull). The sidebar count staleness and Gap A are local refresh/hydration bugs that no subscription will fix — they need the triggers below.

## Fix plan

1. **Debounced recount triggers** — add a `scheduleRecount()` helper (1s debounce) in `savedViewStore` calling `hydrateCounts(userId)`, wired to:
   - taskStore mutations: `createTask`, `updateTask`, `deleteTask`, `addLabel`, `removeLabel` (after the SQLite write)
   - the Realtime batch flush in `App.tsx` (~line 286, where `flushRealtime` is scheduled)
   - `window.api.onTasksChanged` (WAL watcher handler, App.tsx:303–318) — covers local-MCP writes
   Cost: N saved views × one indexed SQL count, debounced — negligible.
2. **Cross-project task hydration for the open view (Gap A)** — on SavedViewListView mount, hydrate tasks for all projects (loop `hydrateAllForProject` over `selectActiveProjects`, or add a `tasks:findAllForUser` repository method + store action). Alternative: a repository-level `findMatchingTasks(filter_config)` mirroring `countMatchingTasks` so the view queries SQL directly instead of relying on store completeness.
3. **Gap B** — depends on task 4c89a910 Part 3 (task_labels targeted pull on Realtime task events). Reference it; don't duplicate the work here.

## Edge cases

- Recount must also fire on task archive/unarchive and project archive (tasks leave the filter set).
- Per-view counts respect the same filter semantics as `countMatchingTasks` — no separate logic.
- Don't recount while the saved view screen has unsaved filter edits (it temporarily overwrites `activeViewFilterConfig`; the unmount cleanup already re-runs `hydrateCounts`).

## Tests

- savedViewStore: `scheduleRecount` debounces (N rapid mutations → 1 `countMatching` IPC per view).
- Integration: create a task with a label matching a saved view → sidebar count increments within ~1–2s without visiting the view.
- SavedViewRepository: `countMatchingTasks` already covered; add a case for label-filtered config.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Creating/completing/labelling a task anywhere updates affected sidebar view counts within ~2s
- [ ] An open saved view shows a newly matching task from ANY project (incl. never-visited ones) without remount
- [ ] MCP-created task with a matching label appears in the open view live once 4c89a910 lands
- [ ] No recount storms (debounced; counts are single indexed SQL queries)

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-still-broken-in-code — recount call sites and the mount-time hydration gap confirmed by reading SavedViewListView.tsx / savedViewStore.ts / ipc-handlers.ts:1222. Related: 4c89a910 (Realtime coverage), 8b6b6b3d (labels-in-view chips).

stories.title: add filters and full row details on archive
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: d6e06073-758e-40c9-9fa3-db75fb63db91 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Add filtering (by project, label, priority, due date, keyword) and richer row details (priority badge, label chips, due date) to the Archive view.

## Why

The archive view currently shows only task title, status icon, and completed date. Users cannot find specific archived tasks without manually scrolling. Other views (project list, My Day, saved views) all have `FilterBar` and full row metadata — the archive should be at parity.

## Current behavior (verified, file:line)

`src/renderer/src/features/views/ArchiveView.tsx`:
- Line 13: component opens, no filter state
- Lines 35–56: `groupedByProject` memo — no filtering beyond `is_archived === 1`
- Lines 312–373: task row renders only `StatusButton` (324) + `title` (333) + `completed_date` (335–340) — no priority, no labels, no due_date
- No `FilterBar`, no `taskLabels` usage, no `hydrateAllTaskLabels` call

Available building blocks:
- `src/renderer/src/shared/components/FilterBar.tsx` — accepts `labels`, `showProjectFilter`, `showSort`; reads filter state from `useLabelStore`; can be embedded unchanged
- `PriorityBadge` (`shared/components/PriorityBadge.tsx`, used in TaskRow.tsx:557), `LabelChip` (used in TaskRow.tsx:562–574)
- `hydrateAllTaskLabels(projectId)` (`taskStore.ts:664`) → `labels.findTaskLabelsByProject(projectId)` (`LabelRepository.ts:415`) — the SQL has no `is_archived` filter, so it already returns labels for archived tasks when called per-project

## Implementation guide

1. **Hydrate labels for all relevant projects** — in `ArchiveView`, after `groupedByProject` is derived:
   ```tsx
   const { hydrateAllTaskLabels } = useTaskStore()
   const taskLabels = useTaskStore((s) => s.taskLabels)
   useEffect(() => {
     for (const g of groupedByProject) hydrateAllTaskLabels(g.project.id)
   }, [groupedByProject, hydrateAllTaskLabels])
   ```
2. **Apply filters** — read filter selectors from `useLabelStore` (`selectActiveLabelFilters`, `selectFilterMode`, `selectPriorityFilters`, `selectDueDatePreset`, `selectDueDateRange`, `selectKeyword`) and apply inside a `filteredGroupedByProject` memo, using the same pattern as `TaskListView.tsx:183–217` (including `matchesDueDateFilter` from `shared/utils/dueDateFilter`).
3. **Mount FilterBar** above the grouped list:
   ```tsx
   <FilterBar labels={useLabelStore(s => Object.values(s.labels))} showProjectFilter showSort={false} />
   ```
4. **Enrich the task row** — after the title span add: `PriorityBadge` when `task.priority > 0`; due date (`text-[10px] font-bold uppercase tracking-widest text-muted/60`) when `task.due_date && !task.completed_date`; `LabelChip` per entry in `taskLabels[task.id] ?? []`.
5. **Project filter** — with `showProjectFilter`, exclude tasks via `selectProjectFilters` (same pattern as TaskListView.tsx:201).

## Edge cases

- Archived project with zero tasks: group header must still appear after filtering (so the user can see the project is archived).
- Label hydration is async — render rows without chips until hydration completes (chips appear when ready; no spinner).
- `filterMode` (AND vs OR) must be respected via the same `matchesLabelFilter` logic as TaskListView.
- `useLabelStore` filter state is shared across views — clearing filters in archive clears them globally (existing app behaviour).

## Tests

`src/renderer/src/features/views/ArchiveView.test.tsx` (create):
- PriorityBadge renders only when `priority > 0`
- LabelChip renders per hydrated label
- Priority filter excludes wrong-priority tasks; project filter excludes filtered-out projects
- Group header still renders when project has zero tasks after filtering

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] FilterBar appears above the archive list with Project, Priority, Label, Due Date, Keyword filters
- [ ] Each row shows: status icon, title, priority badge (if any), label chips (if any), due date or completed date
- [ ] Filtering reduces visible tasks across all project groups; clearing restores all
- [ ] Archived-project group headers stay visible even when all their tasks are filtered out

## Status check (2026-06-10)

stories.title: MCP creation is not part of the activity in task details
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 07a1f88a-0aac-42cb-88c6-5a7530ac12b7 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

Tasks created/modified via the **local Electron MCP server** (built to `out/main/mcp-server.js`) produce NO activity-log entries — the Detail panel's Activity tab stays empty for MCP-created tasks. (The **remote MCP edge function** already logs activity correctly.)

## Repro

Using the local MCP (stdio, shares the SQLite DB):
```json
{ "tool": "create_task", "args": { "title": "Test", "project_id": "<id>" } }
```
Open the task in the app → Activity tab → empty (no "created" entry).

## Expected

Every MCP write operation produces an `activity_log` entry identical to what the renderer produces for the same action.

## Root cause (verified)

The local MCP server (`src/main/mcp-server.ts`) never calls `repos.activityLog.create(...)` in any handler. Compare:

- `create_task` (mcp-server.ts:647–664): calls `repos.tasks.create(...)` and returns — no activity call.
- Remote edge function (`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts:796–808`): calls `await logActivity(task.id, userId, 'created', null, null, projectId)`.

The local `activity_log` SQLite table (migrations.ts:113–123) has no `project_id` column (unlike Supabase), and `ActivityLogRepository.create` (line 29) inserts `(id, task_id, user_id, action, old_value, new_value, created_at)` — so logging is structurally possible locally; it just isn't called.

Affected local handlers: `create_task`, `assign_label_to_task`, `remove_label_from_task`, `complete_task`, `reopen_task`, `set_task_priority`, `set_task_due_date`, `set_task_description`, `archive_task`, `unarchive_task`, `duplicate_task`, `create_subtask`.

## Fix plan

1. In `src/main/mcp-server.ts`, add a helper near the handlers:
   ```ts
   function logActivity(taskId: string, userId: string, action: string, oldValue?: string | null, newValue?: string | null) {
     try {
       repos.activityLog.create({ id: randomUUID(), task_id: taskId, user_id: userId, action, old_value: oldValue ?? null, new_value: newValue ?? null })
     } catch (e) { console.error('[MCP] activity log failed:', e) }
   }
   ```
2. Call it after each mutating operation, mirroring the action strings + old/new values used by the remote edge function (`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts:806–1012`):
   - `create_task` → `logActivity(task.id, user.id, 'created')`
   - `complete_task` / `reopen_task` → `'status_changed'` with old/new status names
   - `assign_label_to_task` → `'label_added'`, `newValue = label.name`; `remove_label_from_task` → `'label_removed'`
   - priority/due-date/description/archive handlers → matching action strings
3. Do NOT pass `project_id` — the local table has no such column.

## Edge cases

- `activityLog.create` can throw on FK violation (task deleted concurrently) — wrap in try/catch, log to stderr, never fail the tool call.
- Action strings must match the renderer's conventions exactly so `DetailActivityLog` renders them identically.

## Tests

- `ActivityLogRepository` test: after the MCP `create_task` flow, an entry with `action = 'created'` exists for the task.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

PARTIALLY fixed @ HEAD d4c9f69 — remote edge function logs activity; the local MCP server logs nothing for any write operation. Note: even after this fix, activity rows written remotely for personal projects don't flow down to the desktop (separate task 4c89a910).

stories.title: MCP write tools return assigned/ok=true without verifying the side effect (silent data drop)
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 41183299-ae74-466e-abf1-81df4d984617 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

`assign_label_to_task` in the **remote MCP edge function** returns `{ assigned: true }` even when the underlying `task_labels` upsert silently failed (RLS rejection, FK violation). The AI caller cannot distinguish real success from a silent drop.

> **Scope narrowed 2026-06-10:** the original report described this pattern as universal across the edge function's write tools. Most have since been hardened — `update_task`, `set_task_priority`, `set_task_due_date`, `set_task_description`, `set_task_recurrence`, `add_task_to_my_day`, `archive_task`, `unarchive_task`, `complete_task`, `snooze_task` all now `if (!result) throw new Error('Task not found: …')` or return the full updated object. The remaining silent-drop risk is isolated to `addLabel` / `assign_label_to_task` (and `remove_label_from_task` returning `{ removed: false }` instead of throwing).

## Repro

1. Call `assign_label_to_task` with a `label_id` whose RLS policy blocks the insert (e.g. a label owned by another user).
2. Tool returns `{ assigned: true, task_id, label_id }`.
3. `get_task` → the `labels` array does NOT contain the label.

## Expected

Return `{ assigned: true }` only when the row is confirmed present; otherwise throw (`isError: true`) so the AI knows the action didn't land.

## Root cause (verified)

`TaskRepo.addLabel` at `supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts:304–307`:

```ts
async addLabel(taskId: string, labelId: string) {
  await this.client.from('task_labels').upsert({ task_id: taskId, label_id: labelId }, { onConflict: 'task_id,label_id' })
  await this.refreshLabelNames(taskId)
}
```

The upsert's `{ data, error }` return is discarded. The handler (lines 1001–1006) returns `{ assigned: true }` unconditionally.

Secondary fragile pattern: `TaskRepo.update()` (lines 235–242) returns `undefined` on error instead of throwing — currently mitigated by `if (!result) throw` at every call site, but new callers can silently regress.

## Fix plan

1. **`TaskRepo.addLabel` (index.ts:304):** capture and throw on error:
   ```ts
   async addLabel(taskId: string, labelId: string) {
     const { error } = await this.client.from('task_labels').upsert(
       { task_id: taskId, label_id: labelId }, { onConflict: 'task_id,label_id' })
     if (error) throw new Error(`Failed to assign label: ${error.message}`)
     await this.refreshLabelNames(taskId)
   }
   ```
2. **Optional verify-after-write** in `assign_label_to_task`: after `addLabel`, fetch the task's labels and confirm `label_id` is present; throw if not.
3. **`remove_label_from_task` (lines 1008–1013):** change `return { removed: false }` on error to a thrown Error so AI callers can't ignore the flag.

## Edge cases

- Already-assigned label: `onConflict` upsert succeeds with no error → still returns success. Correct.
- FK violation (label_id not in user_labels): must throw clearly.
- Deploying the edge function: `supabase functions deploy mcp` — coordinate with any other pending edge-function changes.

## Tests

Integration test mocking `supabase.from('task_labels').upsert` to return `{ error: { message: 'FK violation' } }` → assert the handler throws.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

PARTIALLY fixed @ HEAD d4c9f69 — write tools generally hardened; `addLabel`/`assign_label_to_task` (and `remove_label_from_task`'s soft-false) still silent-drop. Much narrower than the original 8KB description suggested.

SCOPE GUARD: this story touches supabase/functions/ and/or Supabase data. Make the CODE changes and tests only. Do NOT run `supabase functions deploy`, do NOT run SQL against production, do NOT perform any data backfill — those are manual user steps after review.

Before marking passes: true: read ui-reference.md and debug-learnings.md. Write tests for any new repository methods or utility functions. Run npm run test — all existing and new tests must pass. Run npm run typecheck — zero errors.
